newsitem.title: USA: ConEd urges N.Y. power customers to limit usage.
newsitem.headline: ConEd urges N.Y. power customers to limit usage.

text.p: Consolidated Edison of New York said Wednesday it is urging its electricity customers in parts of Queens to reduce their electricity usage due to the unrelenting heat in the area.
Operators are currently making repairs to four electrical feeder cables in the Richmond Hill network and three cables in Flushing, the utility said.
Nearly 170,000 customers are served by the Flushing and Richmond Hill networks.
ConEd said it is anticipating yet another record-high peak demand today as temperatures hover in the 90s degrees F.
On Tuesday, ConEd set an electric demand record of 11,013 megawatts (MW) between 1500 EDT and 1600 EDT, replacing the previous record of 10,805 MW set on August 2, 1995.
The utility on Tuesday reduced voltage in the Richmond Hill area by eight percent to help relieve the electrical load. A reduction may soon be necessary in the Flushing area, the utility said.
The utility added that there is the potential of additional feeder cable problems in other parts of New York City and Westchester County.
